ruling.recommended_action: Send the case file to a human reviewer: the GPS track must be reconciled with the metered 10.10 km billed (F7) versus the 8.0 km recorded (F2) before any excess-distance refund can be calculated under RD-2; the uncovered final 4 minutes of the trip are missing from the record. No driver account flag on this record (no upheld route deviation, RD-6 not met; rider withdrew the request).
ruling.reasoning:
The safety screen finds nothing: the chat is a pickup note and a route request [F8][F9][F10], and the driver's post-trip statement is a factual denial [F12]; the complaint [F1]-adjacent narrative alleges only an unrequested detour, so safety_concern = none.

The trace marks the GPS coverage element failed: the track's last sample is 4 min 0 s before 14:33:55, i.e. the final stretch of the trip is unrecorded and cannot be measured [F1][TH-4]. That alone is an outcome-relevant gap: I cannot tell whether the missing tail accounts for the difference between the metered 10.10 km billed [F7] and the 8.0 km the trace records [F2]. Under TH-4 missing records are escalated and favour neither party, so evidence_status = insufficient.

The route picture is internally inconsistent in a way that blocks the RD-2 arithmetic. The whole-trip deviation on the trace is only +0.3 km, inside the 1 km tolerance [F2][RD-1], while the fare bills an excess of 2.41 km / $3.40 [F5][F7]. The off-route segment 14:27–14:29 is real and fully recorded — 1.90 km driven against 0.67 km optimal, +1.23 km [F4] — but no rider message precedes it: the only route message, the rider's 14:29 request to go via Canning Lane [F10], post-dates the segment start at 14:27 [F4][F10], and the driver's post-trip explanation [F12] is not notice [RD-5]. The driver expressly concedes no notice (C4 conceded) and no traffic reason (C3 conceded) [F13][F14][F15][F16][RD-4], so the segment would count under RD-2 if the record settled the distance.

It does not settle it. The refund base is disputed: the metered excess of $3.40 [F5] rests on 2.41 km of unbilled-vs-billed distance, larger than either the +0.3 km whole-trip figure [F2] or the 1.23 km segment [F4]; and if the missing tail were counted, the excess-billed line changes. Because the shortfall in the record is exactly the distance measure the refund turns on, the pure measure depends on a record a clause needs and the trace orders escalate [F1][F7][RD-2][TH-4]. Profiles (rider clean [F17]; driver's single upheld dispute being neither route nor no-show [F18]) never decide the case [RD-6].
ruling.escalation_reason: segment finding undetermined for F4; evidence insufficient: GPS trace does not cover the whole trip — last sample 4 min 0 s before 14:33:55 (F1) — so the final stretch cannot be measured and the gap in distance between the 8.0 km recorded (F2) and the 10.10 km metered/billed with its $3.40 excess line (F5, F7) cannot be resolved; the excess-distance refund under RD-2 cannot be computed on this record.

segment_findings.reason: Segment 14:27–14:29 drove 1.90 km where the optimal route covers 0.67 km (+1.23 km) [F4]. The complete timestamped chat contains no rider message before 14:27: the only route message is the rider's 14:29 request to go via Canning Lane [F10], which post-dates the start of the segment and so is not consent to it under RD-5; the driver's post-trip statement of a GPS reroute [F12] is not prior notice. No traffic reason exists [F13][F14][F15][F16][RD-4], so nothing exempts it. The rider's 14:29 message names 'Canning Lane', a place the car is not recorded as reaching, and the roads listed for this segment are CANTONMENT ROAD / LIM TECK KIM ROAD / BERNAM STREET / ANSON ROAD / MAXWELL ROAD / WALLICH STREET / CECIL STREET [F4]: if the words are read as a stop/route agreement, no record ties it to this segment, so its exemption status cannot be settled and the finding is undetermined [RD-5][RD-3]. The undetermined finding bears on the RD-2 amount, which is itself unresolvable on the incomplete trace [F1][TH-4].

rejected_claims.reason: The +0.3 km whole-trip deviation [F2] is inside the 1 km tolerance [RD-1], but the refund rests on the separately measured off-route segment [F4]; the claim is noted, not applied, because the trace's coverage failure [F1] prevents the RD-2 measure from being fixed.

Not applied to a refund calculation: no driver message appears before the 14:27 segment start [F9][F11] and the post-trip statement is not notice [F12][RD-5], but the RD-2 amount the notice point feeds into cannot be computed on a track that ends 4 minutes early [F1][TH-4].

Accepted as the reason for escalation rather than a basis for refund: the 8.0 km recorded [F2] and the 10.10 km metered [F7] cannot be reconciled because the trace is incomplete [F1], so the shortfall is undecidable [TH-4][RD-1].

The $3.40 excess line [F5] is a fare fact, but its 2.41 km exceeds both the +0.3 km recorded [F2] and the 1.23 km segment [F4], and with the final stretch unrecorded [F1] it cannot be upheld as the RD-2 excess distance fare; no refund is ordered [RD-2][TH-4].

No account flag is available: the driver's single upheld dispute is expressly not a route or no-show finding [F18], so RD-6's precondition of an upheld route deviation in the last 90 days is not met [RD-6].

The tolerance reading against the whole-trip figure [F2] does not dismiss the case, since RD-2 weighs the km of each segment not exempt under RD-3 / RD-5, and no exemption covers the 14:27–14:29 segment [F4][RD-1][RD-2].
The rider's 14:29 message [F10] is indeed not consent to the 14:27–14:29 segment, but that makes the segment unexcused, not unrefundable; it cannot be used to dismiss the claim [F4][F10][RD-5].
The incomplete track [F1] is a reason to escalate, not to presume in the driver's favour; missing records favour neither party [TH-4].

The conflict between the 8.0 km recorded [F2] and the 10.10 km metered [F7] is a record gap, but the record does not thereby settle the deviation in the driver's favour; the gap itself is the ground of escalation [F1][TH-4].
Profiles are background only: neither the rider's clean record [F17] nor the driver's non-route upheld dispute [F18] decides any element [RD-6].
